info.title: WorkwrK API
info.description: WorkwrK public REST API: programmatic access to the operating-system spine. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer wk_live_...`. Rate limits are enforced per key. A signed-in session also works, for the workspace's Owner and Admins only. Webhooks: every delivery is a POST carrying X-Workwrk-Event, X-Workwrk-Delivery, X-Workwrk-Timestamp and X-Workwrk-Signature: t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature>. To check one, compute HMAC-SHA256 with the subscription's secret (the whsec_ value shown once when it was made or its secret rotated) as the key over <timestamp>.<raw request body>, as lowercase hex, and compare it with v1 in constant time. Refuse a timestamp more than five minutes old. An older subscription may still sign with the SHA-256 of its secret, as lowercase hex, as the key: GET /api/webhooks says which in `signing`, and rotating its secret moves it to the secret itself. The body's `id` is the delivery's id, the same as X-Workwrk-Delivery, and every try of one delivery carries the same `id`, so a receiver can drop a delivery it already has: a delivery whose answer was never recorded is sent again.

bearerAuth.description: Create an API key at /settings/api. Format: `wk_live_<token>`. Scopes: READ, WRITE, ADMIN. Rate-limited per minute and per day.

manager.description: The person they report to, or null.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

period.description: The month the reading is for, YYYY-MM. Readings stored before under other keys (such as 2026-W33 or 2026-Q3) keep them, and drive no goal.

date.description: The due date, or null when the task has none.

status.description: The task's status as its List stores it. Each List keeps its own set of statuses, so there is no fixed list; a List nobody has changed uses the three in `examples`. Null when the task has no status.

priority.description: Null when the task has no priority.

slaHours.description: The hours it was given, or null. Nothing escalates a task when it passes.

assigneeId.description: The task's main assignee, or null when nobody is assigned.

escalatedAt.description: In the list only. Set on tasks carried over from the old task system; nothing sets it now.

_count.description: How many compliance records and assignments the SOP has.

token.description: The secret in the join link. Treat it as a password.

acceptUrl.description: The join link to send the person.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, revoked or unknown API key.

Forbidden.description: The key lacks the scope this endpoint requires, the workspace is suspended or cancelled, or the signed-in person is not the workspace's Owner or an Admin.

RateLimited.description: Per-minute or per-day rate limit for this key exceeded.

400.description: status is not one of the listed values

post.summary: Invite a person into the org
post.description:
Creates a pending invitation and returns its join link (`acceptUrl`) for you to send. Answers 409 when the email is already in the workspace or already invited. The email must use one of the workspace's invite domains, when it has any.

Requires a key with the **ADMIN** scope.

firstName.description: Kept on the invitation, so the join form starts filled in. The person can change it when they accept.

lastName.description: Kept on the invitation, so the join form starts filled in. The person can change it when they accept.

accessLevel.description: Read only from a signed-in Owner's or Admin's session, and never above their own level. With an API key the person is invited as an Employee and this field is ignored.

400.description: email is missing, uses a domain the workspace does not invite from, or roleId or departmentId is not this workspace's

403.description: The key lacks the ADMIN scope, the workspace is suspended or cancelled, the signed-in person may not invite, or the workspace has no free seat for another person (`code` is `seat_limit`).

409.description: The email is already in the workspace, or an invitation to it is pending

post.description:
Post a KPI value from a connected tool. There is one reading per KPI, person and month. A new reading answers 201. The same number again answers 200 and changes nothing, so a retried call is safe: only what you send is compared, the number and, when you send one, targetValue. A different number answers 200 and replaces the reading while its month is open (this month or last month, in any timezone); it goes back to Pending, since a manager's approval was of the old number. A reading with no number yet (a month someone saved in the app with this KPI left blank) is filled in any month, as a new reading is. For a closed month a different number answers 409 with the reading's `id`, and the reading stays as it is. A reading that changes something fires the `kpi.recorded` webhook and recomputes the person's composite score.

Requires a key with the **WRITE** scope (ADMIN satisfies every scope).

period.description: The month the reading is for, written YYYY-MM. Goals read only month keys, so any other key is refused with a 400, and so is a month that has not started yet. Readings stored before under other keys (such as 2026-W33 or 2026-Q3) are still listed, and drive no goal.

actualValue.description: A number, or a string of one.

targetValue.description: Optional: the line the number is scored against, in place of the KPI's own target. For a qualitative KPI, 0 or less is read as no target sent: the KPI's own target rating is used, or else the top of its 1 to 5 scale.

200.description: A reading for this KPI, person and month was there: the same number, unchanged, or a different number that replaced it

400.description: kpiId, userId, period or actualValue is missing; actualValue or targetValue is not a number; or period is not a month written YYYY-MM, or is a month that has not started

404.description: The KPI, or the person, is not in this workspace

409.description: The month is closed and its reading holds a different number (or a different target from the targetValue you sent), which stays as it is. `code` is `kpi_month_closed` and `id` is the reading's id.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

x-events.name: kpi.recorded
x-events.description: Fired when a KPI reading is logged through this API (POST /kpi-records) or an integration.

x-events.name: task.created
x-events.description: Fired for a task added to a List in the app, a task made through this API (POST /tasks) or an integration, a task an automation's Create a task step makes, and a task Ask AI or an AI teammate makes when asked to create one. Not fired for tasks that arrive any other way: copies (duplicating a task, a List or a Space), tasks from a template, the next task of a repeating task, tasks an SOP adds, a form response that makes a task, meeting action items, quick add from My work, tasks a workflow makes, and imports.

x-events.name: task.status_changed
x-events.description: Fired when a task's status changes: one task edited in the app or by an AI teammate, a bulk edit, or an automation step. Carries previousStatus.

x-events.name: task.assignee_changed
x-events.description: Fired when a task's main assignee changes: one task edited in the app or by an AI teammate, a bulk edit, or an automation step. Carries previousAssigneeId.

x-events.name: task.field_changed
x-events.description: Fired once for each field a change touches (title, priority, dates and the List's own fields): one task edited in the app or by an AI teammate, a bulk edit, an AI field fill, or an automation's Set a field step. One edit of one task fires it for at most 20 fields; a change to more fields than that sends the first 20 only.

x-webhook-signature.key: The subscription's secret (whsec_...), shown once when the subscription is made or its secret rotated.
x-webhook-signature.olderSubscriptions: A subscription whose `signing` is legacy_hash (GET /api/webhooks) is signed with the SHA-256 of its secret, as lowercase hex, as the key. Rotating its secret (PATCH /api/webhooks with rotateSecret: true) moves it to the secret itself.
x-webhook-signature.unreadableSubscriptions: A subscription whose `signing` is unreadable has a secret this server can't open right now, so nothing is sent to it: its deliveries are held, not lost, and tried again every 15 minutes until the secret can be opened or is rotated.
